explanation.headline: Neutral · 41/100
explanation.body: The composite score is 41/100, in the Neutral band. Long-term valuation is unavailable, while current market conditions read 41/100 (Mixed). The score summarizes historical relative attractiveness across four categories; it is not an objective measure of intrinsic value.

supporting.name: NASDAQ Composite RSI (14-day)
supporting.text: RSI (14) sits in the 16th percentile over its 20.0-year window and scores 84/100, fearful or trend-supportive conditions.

supporting.name: CNN Fear & Greed Index
supporting.text: Fear & Greed scores 68/100, fearful or trend-supportive conditions.

contradicting.name: Cboe NASDAQ-100 Volatility Index (VXN)
contradicting.text: VXN sits in the 84th percentile over its 20.0-year window and scores 16/100, complacent, overbought, or weak-trend conditions.

contradicting.name: NASDAQ-100 Constituents Above 200-day Average
contradicting.text: Market breadth sits in the 22th percentile over its 5.2-year window and scores 22/100, narrow participation.

conflicts: The components disagree materially: RSI (14) scores 84/100 while VXN scores 16/100.
data_notes: Market breadth uses the current S&P 500 constituent list across history. The series is survivorship-biased and is not a fully representative point-in-time history.
The Buffett Indicator is displayed as supplementary evidence and carries zero weight in the composite.
CNN Fear & Greed, when available, is transformed directly (100 - index) rather than percentile-ranked.

No free long-term valuation series exists for the NASDAQ Composite (CAPE covers the S&P 500 only, and no NASDAQ forward-P/E feed is configured). The NASDAQ composite therefore reweights its categories to sentiment (0.6) and breadth (0.4) and reads current market conditions, not long-term valuation.
One or more percentiles use a shorter window than the 20-year default because the available history is shorter. The component cards disclose the window actually used.
explanation.disclaimer: This dashboard is a historical relative-attractiveness summary, not a forecast, an intrinsic-value estimate, or an automated buy/sell signal. A low score is not a sell instruction and a high score is not a buy instruction.

indicators.name: Buffett Indicator
indicators.description: U.S. listed equity market capitalization as a percentage of nominal GDP.
indicators.source_name: World Bank (market capitalization of listed domestic companies / GDP)
indicators.methodology: Market capitalization of listed domestic companies as a percentage of GDP, as published by the World Bank from World Federation of Exchanges data. The series is shown as supplementary evidence and carries zero weight in the composite.
indicators.limitations: Annual frequency with a substantial publication lag. Coverage is listed domestic companies, not every U.S.-listed issuer, and U.S. companies earn significant revenue abroad. It is supplementary evidence, not a timing tool or a fourth valuation vote. It measures the whole U.S. listed market, not the NASDAQ alone, so the same series is shown in the S&P 500 and NASDAQ views.

indicators.name: Equity Risk Premium (NASDAQ-100 proxy)
indicators.description: The NASDAQ-100 trailing earnings yield minus the 10-year Treasury yield.
indicators.source_name: NASDAQ-100 trailing P/E (daily snapshots) + U.S. Treasury 10-year yield
indicators.methodology: Trailing earnings yield (100 / the NASDAQ-100 trailing P/E, read daily from Yahoo Finance's QQQ figure) minus the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield. Both legs are nominal. The P/E is never forward-looking and never taken from the S&P 500.
indicators.limitations: No free source publishes NASDAQ-100 earnings history, so this series starts on the first day the snapshot job ran and grows by one observation per trading day. Its score is withheld until the history is long enough for a meaningful percentile. ETF-reported P/Es are approximate and are not revised.

indicators.name: CNN Fear & Greed Index
indicators.description: CNN Business's composite measure of market fear and greed, on a 0-100 scale.
indicators.methodology: CNN Fear & Greed Index on its published 0-100 scale. The component is contrarian: score = 100 - index. Fear can create opportunity but is not proof of undervaluation.
indicators.limitations: No public authorized API is bundled. The indicator stays unavailable unless an authorized feed is configured. A separate VIX/RSI sentiment proxy is displayed and explicitly labeled; it is not substituted for CNN data. CNN Fear & Greed measures the broad U.S. market, so the same series is shown in the S&P 500 and NASDAQ views.
indicators.unavailable_reason: Requires an authorized CNN Fear & Greed feed. Set FEAR_GREED_CSV_URL or import a licensed CSV. An independent daily Fear & Greed index is available from FearGreedChart.com (free API, history from Oct 2016, CORS-enabled). A labeled VIX/RSI proxy is shown in the summary.

indicators.name: Cboe NASDAQ-100 Volatility Index (VXN)
indicators.description: The options-implied expected 30-day volatility of the NASDAQ-100, the NASDAQ counterpart of the VIX.
indicators.methodology: Daily closes of the Cboe NASDAQ-100 Volatility Index. The score is the historical percentile of the current level over the configured window.
indicators.limitations: Elevated VIX is not proof that equities are cheap. VIX measures implied volatility and can remain elevated during prolonged drawdowns. It is a supplementary sentiment and risk indicator.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite RSI (14-day)
indicators.description: Wilder's 14-day Relative Strength Index of the NASDAQ Composite.
indicators.source_name: NASDAQ Composite daily closes (^IXIC), Wilder RSI
indicators.methodology: Wilder's RSI with a 14-period lookback, computed from daily NASDAQ Composite closing prices. The component is contrarian: lower RSI maps to a higher score through an inverse historical percentile. Conventional 30/70 reference levels are displayed.
indicators.limitations: RSI is a price-momentum measure, not a fundamental valuation measure. It can remain oversold or overbought for extended periods. The 30/70 levels are conventions, not statistically validated thresholds.

latest.source: NASDAQ Composite daily closes / Wilder RSI

scored.source: NASDAQ Composite daily closes / Wilder RSI

indicators.name: NASDAQ vs 200-day Moving Average
indicators.description: The percentage distance between the NASDAQ Composite and its 200-trading-day simple moving average.
indicators.methodology: Percentage deviation of the NASDAQ Composite close from its 200-trading-day simple moving average. The component is trend-oriented: higher deviation maps to a higher score through a historical percentile. A zero line marks the moving average.
indicators.limitations: This is primarily a trend indicator, not a valuation measure. A market above its 200-day average can still be expensive, and a market below it can still be cheap.

indicators.name: NASDAQ-100 Constituents Above 200-day Average
indicators.description: The percentage of current NASDAQ-100 constituents trading above their own 200-day averages.
indicators.source_name: Yahoo Finance adjusted prices for current NASDAQ-100 constituents
indicators.methodology: For each trading day, the percentage of the current NASDAQ-100 constituent list whose adjusted close exceeds its own 200-trading-day simple moving average. The component is trend-oriented: higher breadth maps to a higher score through a historical percentile.
indicators.limitations: Current constituents are used for the whole history, so the series has survivorship bias. The list is bundled with the project (or read from NASDAQ_CONSTITUENTS_URL) and the index is reconstituted every December. History is limited to the configured lookback (six years by default).
indicators.status_message: Computed 1307 daily breadth observations from 101 symbols

indicators.name: Equal-weight vs Cap-weight NASDAQ-100
indicators.description: Cumulative relative performance of the equal-weighted NASDAQ-100 (QQEW) versus the cap-weighted NASDAQ-100 (QQQ).
indicators.methodology: The ratio of QQEW (First Trust NASDAQ-100 Equal Weighted ETF) adjusted close to QQQ (Invesco QQQ, cap-weighted NASDAQ-100) adjusted close. Both series are normalized to 100 at their common start. Scoring uses the trailing 252-day relative return.
indicators.limitations: ETF-based proxy, not an official total-return index. QQEW began trading in 2006. The ratio reflects concentration in mega-caps but has other drivers.
